name: Apply ESOI to a Project
description: ESOI is a way to turn what someone means into a structure that keeps serving that meaning while both change. People and agents learn it and find their way around it; a project's records and code stay true and lean; evidence decides which way of doing each job is best; and that choice reaches the programs that run, without anyone rewriting them. A project can apply it with documents alone or add the tools, which check the records and move each selection to the measured winner.
purpose: Turn a project's intent into specifications that are checked, measured and selected by metric, so the structure keeps evolving with the intent.
approach: Start from plain documents and templates that anyone can fill in by hand (Understanding), then add checks (Structure), measurement and selection (Optimization) and the carrying of the choice into running programs (Runtime), so the records stay true to the intent.
out_of_scope: Deciding what a project is for: that is the project's own top intent.
milestones: 1. Adoption effort: one recorded newcomer trial applying ESOI from the documents only, and one with the tools.
measures_of_success: A newcomer applies ESOI from the documents alone with few questions, and a project's records pass the structure check. Standing conditions: A person or an agent can specify an intent, compare the alternatives of each solution by metric and let the best one be used, with every part reachable from the specifications.
parameters: The project's own top intent, and which implementations of the building blocks to use.
inputs: A project's intent, in its owner's words.
outputs: Specifications for the project (an intent folder with its five record types), checks and metric results.
effects: None beyond the files the project keeps.
usage_notes: Start from the documents and templates; add the Python tools where checks, measurement and selection should run by themselves.

name: Understanding
description: This is where ESOI meets people and agents. It holds the explanation and templates someone needs to start by hand, the order to work in, the published skill, the standing instructions that make an agent act by the principles, and the pages and searches that put the right records in front of a reader. It improves when the author refines what ESOI says or when readers need something different, even if no code changes.
purpose: Bring ESOI to the people and agents who apply it, in the author's own words, and let each of them find, read and steer the part of a structure in front of them.
approach: Compose the standard, the standing instructions for agents, the readable pages, the review tracker, the search and the local index, each measured and replaceable on its own. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (adoption effort, steps followed, behaviour adherence, judge agreement, glanceability, review coverage, search correctness, index lookup) move when the author changes the skill or when readers need something different, even if no line of code changes; it is the only container whose metric is agreement with a person.
out_of_scope: Keeping records true to the code; measuring alternatives and choosing between them; serving an implementation inside a running program.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
measures_of_success: A newcomer applies ESOI from what Understanding gives alone, an agent acts by the principles, and a reader finds the part of a project that bears on their work. Standing conditions: each part reports on a project in one read-only call.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: what each says about the project.
effects: Reads the project's records and documents; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-understanding", ".")` returns the report of each part.

name: Structure
description: This is the project's own form: the linked records, the template they follow, the map from every file to its purpose, the rules that keep it all in shape, and the budget that keeps the structure from costing more than it returns. It changes when the project's records, template or code change.
purpose: Keep a project's records and code one true and lean structure that says why every part exists and improves itself where it falls short.
approach: Compose the registry of records, the map from files to solutions, the structural check and the budget that keeps the structure proportionate. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (record completeness, navigable records, template agreement, trace completeness, violation detection, cost against catches) move when a project's records, its template or its code change: a new file, a drifted row, a refined field.
out_of_scope: Teaching ESOI and showing records to readers; measuring and selecting implementations; choosing at run time.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
measures_of_success: Every file reaches a solution, every record is complete and every link resolves both ways, and the structural check passes. Standing conditions: each part reports on a project in one read-only call.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: records counted, files unowned, findings by rule and the budget.
effects: Reads the project's records and code; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-structure", ".")` returns the report of each part and whether the coherence gate passes.
change_driver: the system's own data model or code

name: Optimization
description: This is how a project comes to run its best implementations on evidence rather than habit. It runs the shipped code on fixed cases, proves the cases can fail, decides when a run is worth its cost (checking first whether the result is still current and whether others have already measured it), calls winners only beyond the noise, switches the selection, and keeps a before-and-after record of each piece of work. It improves when new implementations, cases or results arrive.
purpose: Make each solution run the implementation the evidence shows is best, with evidence that is trustworthy, current and worth what it cost.
approach: Compose the harness that measures, the decision of when to measure, the leaderboard that judges, the promotion that switches and the record of each piece of work. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (provenance completeness, case discrimination, ranking correctness, staleness precision, public evidence graded, promotion correctness, decisions backed by current results, metric record kept) move when evidence changes: a new arm, a new case set, a new public result. It is the Optimizes in ESOI's name. For ESOI the driver ML task accuracy is read as how accurately evidence is gathered and judged.
out_of_scope: Keeping records true; serving the selected implementation inside a program; teaching.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
measures_of_success: Each solution's selected implementation is the measured winner or a declared tie, on evidence that is current and traceable. Standing conditions: each part reports on a project in one read-only call.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: components measured, what a run costs, the standings, the proposals and the metric readings.
effects: Reads the project's records and results; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-optimization", ".")` returns the report of each part.

name: Runtime
description: This is ESOI inside programs that are running for someone. A program declares its alternatives where its code defines them; each call is served by the selected one; whole programs are assembled from named parts with their environment needs checked; and a system built on the library can show that it meets the library's standard and see how far behind it is.
purpose: Carry ESOI into other people's running programs, so a better measurement changes what runs without anyone editing a call site.
approach: Compose the selection of an implementation per call, the assembly of whole programs from named parts and the check of a consumer's system against the library. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (resolution correctness, assembly cases, consumer soundness) move when the embedding programs, their environments or their pinned versions change, all outside this repository.
out_of_scope: Deciding which implementation is best; keeping the records; teaching.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
measures_of_success: Every switch of an implementation works from configuration alone, a program is assembled from names, and a consumer sees how far its pins trail. Standing conditions: each part reports in one read-only call.
parameters: A solution id to show the parts on.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: the choice for the solution, the names it assembles and the ids a consumer knows.
effects: Imports the chosen implementation lazily; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-runtime", "structure-check")` returns the report of each part.
